newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw seals hotels sale to Bau.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw seals hotels sale to Bau.

text.p: Warsaw municipality signed a final agreement on Tuesday to sell the city's chain of six hotels to Austria's Bau Holding, PAP news agency reported.
Under the accord, announced last month, Bau will pay 72 million zlotys for 80 percent of shares in the Syrena chain and invest an additional 150 million zlotys over the next six years.
"I hope the transaction will please both the city and the hotels' workers," PAP quoted senior Bau official Gernot Leuthmetzer as saying.

Hotel employees will be offered 15 percent of shares in the chain and five percent will be put aside for a government programme to compensate former owners for property confiscated under communist rule.
The Syrena hotels, called Metropol, Saski, Polonia, MdM, Polonia and Nowa Praga, were built under the pre-1989 communist system. With one exception, they are strategically located in the city centre.
The agreement provides for keeping Syrena's employment at the current 500 people during the next three years.
